name: Georgia Marble Festival
customer: Craft fair people, stone people, families
unique: A marble town throwing itself a party, with a Main Street parade, a sculpture symposium, vendors in Lee Newton Park and bus tours into working quarries that supply the stone for the Lincoln Memorial.
buzz: The quarry tour is the reason to go and it sells out. Everything else is a good county festival with better raw material than most.

name: Georgia Marble Story Trail
unique: A self guided trail of sites across Pickens County that explains how the marble under these hills became courthouses, monuments and headstones across the country, from the quarries at Tate and Nelson to the carving sheds and the town squares.
buzz: Nobody expects a marble industry trail in north Georgia and everybody who drives it comes back talking about the sheer scale of the quarry walls.

name: Talking Rock Heritage Days
unique: A small town festival in a town of about seventy people, with craft booths, music and a walk along the old railroad grade past the Trail of Tears mural.
buzz: Tiny, genuine and easy to walk in an hour. The setting does most of the work.

name: Talking Rock Park and Trail of Tears Mural
unique: A pocket park on the old railroad line with a mural about the Cherokee removal that passed through this valley, and a paved path that follows the grade the trains used.
buzz: Small, free and honest about what happened here. A good ten minute stop on the way to the mountains.

name: Brasstown Bald
unique: At 4,784 feet the highest ground in Georgia, with an observation deck that shows three states on a clear day, reached by shuttle or a steep half mile trail from the parking lot.
buzz: The view is the whole state in one frame. Locals time visits for the third week of October when the hardwoods turn, and the deck gets cold and windy even in summer.

name: Lake Chatuge and Towns County Beach
dates: Beach Memorial Day to Labor Day
unique: A 7,000 acre TVA reservoir with mountain water clarity, a free county beach with lifeguards, and marinas that rent pontoons for the day.
buzz: The water is cold and clean and the mountains come right down to it. Locals swim at the county beach and rent boats when family visits.

name: Georgia Mountain Fair
customer: Families, country music fans, mountain residents
unique: The 76th edition of a mountain fair with a pioneer village of log cabins, a flower show, harness racing and a music hall that has booked country acts for generations.
buzz: The pioneer village is what separates it from a midway fair, and the music schedule draws people from three states. Cool nights make August bearable up here.

name: Hamilton Gardens
unique: Twenty acres of native azaleas, rhododendrons and trillium on a hillside above Lake Chatuge, planted and maintained by a garden club and free to walk.
buzz: The rhododendron bloom in May is the local event. Quiet, terraced and better than most paid gardens in the state.

name: Vogel State Park
unique: One of Georgia's oldest state parks, built around Lake Trahlyta below Blood Mountain, with Civilian Conservation Corps stonework, cabins, a swimming beach and the trailhead for the Blood Mountain loop.
buzz: The CCC stone bridge and the lake are the postcard. Fall weekends fill the campground months ahead, and the lake trail is short enough for small kids.

name: Walasi-Yi Center at Neels Gap
customer: Thru hikers, day hikers, history people
unique: A stone building put up by the Civilian Conservation Corps between 1934 and 1938 that the Appalachian Trail passes straight through, the only structure on the entire 2,190 mile route that the trail goes inside.
buzz: Thru hikers resupply here and leave their boots on the wall. The stonework and the gap itself are worth the stop even if you are only walking a mile.

name: Blood Mountain
dates: Year round, best April to November
unique: The highest point on the Appalachian Trail in Georgia at 4,458 feet, topped with bare granite and a CCC stone shelter from the 1930s, reached by a steep two mile climb from Neels Gap.
buzz: The summit view runs to Atlanta on a clear day. It is a real climb, not a stroll, and the shelter at the top is where everybody eats lunch.

name: Track Rock Gap Petroglyphs
unique: Soapstone boulders carved with concentric circles, animal tracks and human figures by people who lived here centuries before the Cherokee, beside a Forest Service road with a boardwalk and an interpretive sign.
buzz: Nobody knows what the marks mean. It is a five minute stop that people remember for years, and the setting in a gap between two ridges is half the experience.

name: Helton Creek Falls
dates: Year round, road may close in winter
unique: Two waterfalls in a quarter mile, the lower one dropping into a pool shallow enough for kids, at the end of a Forest Service road off Highway 129.
buzz: One of the easiest big waterfall walks in the state. Parking is small, so early is better, and the road is rough enough that low cars scrape.

name: Sorghum Festival
unique: A festival built around a mule drawn sorghum mill pressing cane into syrup over a fire, with biscuits, crafts and clogging on the grounds of the fairgrounds.
buzz: The syrup making is the real thing and you can watch the whole process. Buy a jar before Sunday afternoon, it sells out.

name: Kayak Attack Adventures
unique: A Leesburg outfitter running kayak and canoe trips on Kinchafoonee and Muckalee creeks and the Flint, with shuttles and rentals for people who have never paddled before.
buzz: Reviews praise the shuttle and the patience with beginners. The creeks are narrow, shaded and slow, which is the point.

name: Kinchafoonee Creek
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
unique: A blackwater creek running through cypress and tupelo south of Leesburg, floatable at Highway 32 and other bridges, with sandbars and a redbreast sunfish population that draws fly anglers.
buzz: Anglers who know it call it one of the best small creek float and fish trips in southwest Georgia. You will see more turtles than people.

name: Chehaw Indian Monument
unique: A stone monument on New York Road marking the site of Chehaw, a Creek town that was a trading crossroads until it was burned by militia in 1818, in an attack that caused a national scandal.
buzz: Almost nobody stops and the story is a hard one told in a few lines of bronze. Worth ten minutes if you care how the frontier actually worked.

name: David Bushnell Cenotaph
customer: History of science people, cemetery walkers
unique: A marker in the Warrenton cemetery for David Bushnell, the Connecticut inventor who built the Turtle, the first submarine used in combat, and who spent his last years teaching school in this Georgia town.
buzz: A submarine pioneer's grave in a piney woods town cemetery is exactly the kind of thing nobody believes until they see it. Local teachers use it.

name: Warren County Courthouse Square
unique: A brick courthouse on a square in a town laid out in 1794, with the old stagecoach inn and a block of storefronts around it, in one of the poorest and least visited counties in the state.
buzz: Quiet, handsome and completely untouristed. The square is the whole downtown and it has not been dressed up for visitors.

name: Rocky Comfort Plantation
unique: A private campground and lodge on plantation land near the Ogeechee River with ponds, woods and enough space that groups can take the whole place.
buzz: Basic facilities and total quiet. People book it for reunions and hog hunts rather than a resort weekend.

name: Gordon Train Museum
unique: A small railroad museum in a town named for a railroad man, with a caboose, signals and depot artifacts from the Central of Georgia line that put Gordon on the map.
buzz: Run by volunteers and open when someone is there. Kids climb the caboose and the old timetables are the interesting part.

name: Balls Ferry Park
unique: A public landing on the Oconee River at a crossing that has been used since the 1800s, now a county park with a ramp, picnic tables and room for a crowd.
buzz: The county uses it for river events and everyone else uses it to launch a boat. Peaceful on a weekday, busy when the river is running right.

name: Historic Union Church
unique: A rural church kept by the county historical society, standing in its cemetery outside Irwinton, one of the buildings the local tourism office will open for anyone who calls.
buzz: The kind of place that exists because a handful of families kept it up. Call the number on the county tourism site and someone will meet you.
